title: Reduction of projective space to products of lines
statement: Write, for a scheme $S$ and $m\ge0$, $\mathbf P^m_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,m\};S)$ for the projective space of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and $q_{m,S}:\mathbf P^m_S\to S$ for its structure morphism; so $\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$. For a scheme $T$ define $(\mathbf P^1_T)^n$ with its projection $p_n:(\mathbf P^1_T)^n\to T$ inductively by $(\mathbf P^1_T)^0=T$, $p_0=\mathrm{id}_T$, and $(\mathbf P^1_T)^n=(\mathbf P^1_T)^{n-1}\times_T\mathbf P^1_T$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $p_{n-1}$ and $q_{1,T}$), $p_n=p_{n-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$; this is the $n$-fold fibre product $\mathbf P^1_T\times_T\cdots\times_T\mathbf P^1_T$. Assume that for every scheme $S$ the projection $q_{1,S}:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ satisfies $\mathrm{PBC}$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-property]. Then for every scheme $T$ and every $n\geq0$ the morphisms $p_n:(\mathbf P^1_T)^n\to T$ and $q_{n,T}:\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ are proper and satisfy $\mathrm{PBC}$.

proof.text: *Properness.* $\mathrm{PBC}$ is defined for proper morphisms [def-weil-pbc-property], so we record that every morphism below is proper. $q_{m,S}$ is proper for every $m$ and $S$ [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Isomorphisms are finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite] and finite morphisms are proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. For $p_n$ we argue by induction on $n$: $p_0=\mathrm{id}_T$ is an isomorphism, hence proper; for $n\ge1$, step 4 writes $\mathrm{pr}_1=q_{1,X}\circ\chi$ with $X=(\mathbf P^1_T)^{n-1}$ and $\chi$ an isomorphism, so $\mathrm{pr}_1$ and then $p_n=p_{n-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ are proper as composites of proper morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition].

source.place: Lemma 0A4E (label lemma-finite), proof: a finite morphism is proper (Morphisms, Lemma 01WN); Lemma 0A4F, proof

proof.text: *Composition in terms of $\mathrm{PBC}$.* Let $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$ be proper with $\mathrm{PBC}(u)$ and $\mathrm{PBC}(v)$. By [lemma-weil-pbc-property-iff-acyclicity], $\mathrm{IA}_r(u)$ and $\mathrm{IA}_r(v)$ hold for every prime $r$, i.e. $\mathrm{IA}(u)$ and $\mathrm{IA}(v)$ [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property]; by [prop-weil-pbc-composition-stability], $\mathrm{PBC}(v\circ u)$ holds. This is Stacks Lemma 0A4D, used below repeatedly.

source.place: Lemma 0A4D (label lemma-composition), with the equivalence of Lemma 0A4B used "without further mention"

proof.text: *The case $n=0$.* $p_0=\mathrm{id}_T$ is an isomorphism, and $q_{0,T}:\mathbf P(\{0\};T)\to T$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-zero-isomorphism]. Both are finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite], hence satisfy $\mathrm{PBC}$ [prop-weil-pbc-finite-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 0A4E (label lemma-finite); the source states the symmetric-product argument for $n\ge1$ only, the case $n=0$ is written out here

proof.text: *$\mathrm{PBC}(p_n)$ by induction on $n$.* Let $n\ge1$, assume $\mathrm{PBC}(p_{n-1})$, and put $X=(\mathbf P^1_T)^{n-1}$. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback], applied to the index set $\{0,1\}$ and $g=p_{n-1}:X\to T$, the square formed by $q_{1,X}:\mathbf P^1_X\to X$, $q_{1,T}$, $p_{n-1}$ and the induced map $\mathbf P^1_X\to\mathbf P^1_T$ is cartesian; so there is an isomorphism $\chi:X\times_T\mathbf P^1_T\to\mathbf P^1_X$ over $X$, i.e. $q_{1,X}\circ\chi=\mathrm{pr}_1$ (the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]). Now $\chi$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite], hence $\mathrm{PBC}(\chi)$ [prop-weil-pbc-finite-morphism]; $\mathrm{PBC}(q_{1,X})$ is the hypothesis applied to $S=X$. Step 2 gives $\mathrm{PBC}(\mathrm{pr}_1)$, and step 2 again, with $\mathrm{PBC}(p_{n-1})$, gives $\mathrm{PBC}(p_{n-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_1)=\mathrm{PBC}(p_n)$. With step 3 this proves $\mathrm{PBC}(p_n)$ for all $n\ge0$. (No separate stability of $\mathrm{PBC}$ under base change is needed: the hypothesis is for every base $S$, and is applied to $S=X$; the transport along the isomorphism $\chi$ is the finite case plus composition.)

source.place: Lemma 0A4F, proof, last paragraph ("Applying Lemmas ... and 0A4D one more time"); the source does not spell out the induction, written out here

proof.text: *The symmetric-product morphism.* Let $n\ge1$. The morphism $\sigma_n:(\mathbf P^1_T)^n\to\mathbf P^n_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-properties] is finite [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-finite], hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and $\mathrm{PBC}(\sigma_n)$ holds [prop-weil-pbc-finite-morphism]; it is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-surjective]; and it is a morphism over $T$, $q_{n,T}\circ\sigma_n=p_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-over-base].

source.place: Lemma 0A4F (label lemma-reduce-to-P1), proof, last paragraph ("For every $n \geq 1$ there is a finite surjective morphism ... Applying Lemmas 0A4C, 0A4E, 0A4D one more time")

proof.text: *Cancellation.* For $n\ge1$ apply [lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation] to $(\mathbf P^1_T)^n\xrightarrow{\sigma_n}\mathbf P^n_T\xrightarrow{q_{n,T}}T$: both are proper (steps 1 and 5), $\sigma_n$ is surjective, $\mathrm{PBC}(\sigma_n)$ holds by step 5, and $\mathrm{PBC}(q_{n,T}\circ\sigma_n)=\mathrm{PBC}(p_n)$ by steps 4 and 5. Hence $\mathrm{PBC}(q_{n,T})$. With step 3 for $n=0$, $\mathrm{PBC}(q_{n,T})$ holds for every $n\ge0$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich) as applied in Lemma 0A4F, proof, last paragraph

proof_origin.place: Lemma 0A4F (tag 0A4F, label lemma-reduce-to-P1), proof, last paragraph; with Lemmas 0A4C, 0A4D, 0A4E

split_report.summary: Statement made precise (P^m_S = P({0..m};S) of def-nagata-projective-space-base-change; (P^1_T)^n defined inductively as iterated fibre product with p_n = p_{n-1}∘pr_1; conclusion PBC(p_n) and PBC(q_{n,T}) plus properness, for n≥0); the mechanism ('by repeated base change ... by cancellation along σ_n') moved from the statement into the proof, so σ_n and def-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-morphism left stmt_deps and def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product entered. Proof rewritten in 6 steps following Stacks 0A4F, last paragraph, with 0A4C/0A4D/0A4E: properness; composition in PBC form (composition-stability is stated with IA hypotheses, so the iff lemma is used to convert, which the old proof omitted); n=0 (not covered by the source nor by σ_n, which needs n≥1; new node lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-zero-isomorphism); induction on n using the pullback lemma and the hypothesis for S=(P^1_T)^{n-1} (no base-change stability of PBC needed; the isomorphism χ is handled by the finite case, new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite); σ_n finite, surjective, over T (the last was used but stated nowhere: new node lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-product-over-base); cancellation. Checked: lemma-weil-pbc-cancellation states exactly X-f->Y-h->Z proper, f surjective, PBC(f), PBC(hf) ⇒ PBC(h); prop-weil-pbc-finite-morphism gives PBC for every finite morphism. Mathlib searched three ways: no proper base change.
